newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL-SSAB H1 PROFIT SEEN 27 PCT LOWER.
newsitem.headline: POLL-SSAB H1 PROFIT SEEN 27 PCT LOWER.

text.p: Swedish steel company SSAB was expected to post a profit after financial items of 1.07 billion crowns for the first half of 1997, a Reuters poll of 14 analysts found on Monday.
This would be a fall of 27 percent from the same period a year ago when the company posted a profit after financial items of 1.49 billion crowns.
Forecasts for the first six months of 1997 varied between 935 million crowns and 1.23 billion crowns.
For the full year analysts expected SSAB to post a profit of 2.21 billion crowns which was largely unchanged from forecasts for the full year made at the time of the first quarter repoirt.

Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aragon, Aros, Carnegie, CI Nordic, Den Danske Bank, Den Norske Bank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Enskilda, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, Kleinwort Benson, Matteus, Nordbanken, Nordiska, Paribas, and Swedbank.
SSAB will release its H1 report on Friday, August 15.
